faq.question: Is it ElevenLabs versus Vapi, or do I need both?
faq.answer: They solve different problems. ElevenLabs is a voice (text to speech) layer that makes replies sound human. Vapi is an orchestration platform that runs the live call: turn taking, interruptions, tool calls, and routing. A production agent usually uses a voice layer inside a platform, so it is rarely an either-or choice.

faq.question: What is ElevenLabs actually good at?
faq.answer: Voice quality. Its speech sounds natural across many languages and styles, which keeps callers engaged and builds trust. Where audio realism matters most, it is a strong choice for the voice layer of your agent.

faq.question: What is Vapi actually good at?
faq.answer: Running the conversation. Vapi handles the real-time mechanics of a phone call: detecting speech, managing turns, calling your tools, and holding call state. It is the platform your agent runs on, and it can use different voice providers underneath, including ElevenLabs.

faq.question: Which one should I pick if I only want one?
faq.answer: If you want a working phone agent, start from the orchestration platform (Vapi) and choose a voice layer inside it. ElevenLabs alone will not answer calls or book appointments. The platform is the foundation, the voice is a component within it.

faq.question: Do you build the whole thing or just advise?
faq.answer: We build it. We architect the agent logic (using a model like Claude Opus 4.8 as the build spec), stand it up on Vapi, wire in the right voice layer, and connect your calendar and CRM so calls end in booked outcomes. You get a live agent, not a comparison chart.
